rounds.response:
Problem (2 sentences): Over the next 12–18 months, the sponsor faces operational and reputational risk from AI-assisted decision tools because governance is uneven, recent incidents suggest recurring failure modes, and monitoring is weak. This project will rapidly identify 2–3 near-term, feasible interventions that reduce those highest-impact risks using the internal landscape report and the incident dataset. 

Focused research questions (3–4): Q1: What are the most frequent and highest-impact failure modes in current AI-assisted decisions? Q2: What root causes and governance gaps explain those failures (process, data, human-in-the-loop, or vendor issues)? Q3: Which 2–3 interventions are likely to reduce risk quickly and are feasible within existing resources? Q4: How should the sponsor monitor implementation and detect regressions with lightweight metrics? 

Work packages (3–4) — each sized for three researchers + part-time analyst, tasks 2–3, mapped to questions: WP1 — Rapid evidence synthesis & framing (maps to Q1,Q2): 1) extract and summarize relevant findings from the internal landscape report; 2) classify and timeline recent incidents into failure-mode categories; 3) produce a 1-page risk snapshot. WP2 — Targeted incident analysis (maps to Q1,Q2): 1) clean/annotate the incident dataset (analyst-led); 2) simple root-cause coding and frequency/impact tabulation; 3) short synthesis of immediate risk levers. WP3 — Intervention design & prioritization (maps to Q3): 1) generate candidate interventions (policy, process, tooling, vendor controls); 2) score each by expected risk reduction, cost/effort, and confidence with a simple rubric; 3) recommend 2–3 prioritized interventions with implementation notes. WP4 — Monitoring & decision-support package (maps to Q4,+Q3): 1) define 3–5 pragmatic KPIs and alert triggers; 2) draft a one-page implementation checklist and governance assignment; 3) produce a 1–2 page executive brief with recommended next steps and monitoring dashboard spec. 

All tasks avoid large-scale data builds or complex modeling; deliverables for the sponsor-ready one-pager will be: the concise problem statement, the 3–4 research questions, the prioritized intervention recommendations (2–3) with short rationale, and a simple monitoring plan — I can convert this into a one-page executive brief by end of day.

Over the next 12–18 months the sponsor faces material operational and reputational risk from AI-assisted decision tools because governance is uneven, recent incidents show recurring failure modes, and monitoring is weak; this project will identify 2–3 near-term, feasible interventions that reduce those risks using the internal landscape report and the incident dataset.  
We will answer four plain questions: (1) Which failure modes are most frequent and highest-impact? (2) What root causes and governance gaps drive those failures? (3) Which 2–3 interventions can meaningfully reduce risk quickly and are feasible with current resources? (4) How should the sponsor monitor deployment and detect regressions with lightweight indicators?  
Work packages, deliverables, and 1–3 day tasks (researcher = R, analyst = A): WP1 — Evidence synthesis (deliverable: 1‑page risk snapshot + failure‑mode map) — tasks: R1 review & extract findings from internal report (1–2 days), R2 classify incidents from summary materials (1–2 days), R3 draft 1‑page snapshot (1 day). WP2 — Incident analysis (deliverable: frequency/impact table) — tasks: A1 clean/annotate dataset (analyst-preferred; can be deferred 48 hrs) (1–3 days), R1–R2 code root causes and tabulate counts (1–3 days); WP3 — Intervention design & prioritization (deliverable: scored shortlist of 2–3 interventions with implementation notes) — tasks: R1 generate candidate interventions (1–2 days), R2 apply simple rubric to score risk reduction/cost/confidence (1–2 days), R3 draft implementation notes (1 day). WP4 — Monitoring & decision package (deliverable: 1‑page KPI list + 1‑page executive brief) — tasks: R1 define 3–5 pragmatic KPIs and triggers (1 day), R2 draft dashboard spec and governance assignments (1–2 days), R3 produce final 1–2 page exec brief (1 day).  
Analyst availability note: the analyst is unavailable for two days — tasks flagged above as analyst-preferred (dataset cleaning/annotation and initial coding) should be scheduled after the two-day gap or started in parallel only if the analyst becomes available; researchers can complete WP1 synthesis, candidate interventions (WP3), and KPI drafting (WP4) while dataset work is pending so progress and early outputs continue. Early sponsor-ready products (within ~2 weeks) that do not require full dataset completion: (A) 1‑page risk snapshot + failure‑mode map from WP1, and (B) a scored shortlist of 2–3 candidate interventions with brief implementation notes from WP3.  
Success criteria and progress tracking (draft for memo): Success means the project delivers clear answers to the four questions and supports a leadership decision on 2–3 prioritized interventions that are implementable within current resources and demonstrably reduce risk; success signals are: delivery of the WP1 snapshot and WP3 shortlist (decision‑ready), quantified estimates of expected risk reduction and effort for each recommended intervention, and an agreed 3–5 KPI monitoring plan. Interim milestones: Week 1 — risk snapshot and failure‑mode map (WP1); Week 2 — prioritized shortlist with scoring rubric (WP3) and initial KPI proposals (WP4); Week 3 — final recommendations, monitoring package, and short implementation checklist. Simple indicators to track progress: task board status (To Do / In Progress / Done), completion of the two week‑1/2 deliverables, and a three‑tier health flag for each WP (Green = on track, Amber = at risk, Red = blocked) tied to whether required data/analyst input is available; governance for decisions: two milestone reviews (after Week 1 and Week 3) at which leadership will be asked to approve the recommended 2–3 interventions or request further analysis.

Work‑package → sponsor deliverable → 10‑day vs extended → time bands (three researchers, analyst ≈ half‑day/week): WP1 Evidence synthesis → 1‑page risk snapshot — 10‑day (Days 1–3: R review internal report, classify failure modes; analyst not required); WP2 Incident analysis → preliminary frequency/impact table — 10‑day (Days 3–6: R extract/triage incident summaries), extended (Weeks 2–4: A cleans/annotates dataset and R/A run simple coding & refine numbers — analyst required); WP3 Intervention design → scored shortlist (2–3) — 10‑day (Days 4–8: R generate candidates + apply simple rubric), extended (Weeks 3–4: refine scores with analyst inputs); WP4 Monitoring & brief → KPI list + 1–2 page exec brief — 10‑day (Days 8–10: R draft KPIs and brief), extended (Week 4: finalize dashboard spec/governance).  
Analyst‑required steps (schedule after current 2‑day gap): dataset cleaning/annotation and any quantitative impact estimation or re‑scoring that depends on the full dataset; all other tasks are doable by researchers in 1–3 day chunks so progress continues while analyst is limited.  
Three sponsor‑ready summary formats you can drop into slides or a 1–2 page memo: (A) Comparative table — columns: Intervention | What it fixes | Expected impact (H/M/L) | Effort (Low/Med/High) | Key KPI; (B) Now / Proposed snapshot — left: Top 3 risks today (bullets + example incident); right: 2–3 interventions (bullet each: what changes, who owns it, one KPI); (C) Traffic‑light matrix — rows = interventions, cols = KPIs and readiness; color code Impact vs Effort to show priority.  
If helpful, I can draft the 1–2 page 10‑day memo or a 3‑slide readout in draft form for your review tomorrow morning.

Interventions (comparative, 1–2 sentences each): 1) Targeted second‑review for high‑risk decisions — What it is: require a quick human recheck for AI recommendations that meet a simple risk rule (e.g., high value, regulatory sensitivity, or safety impact); What it fixes & effect: prevents obvious AI errors reaching action and should cut high‑impact operational mistakes quickly; Effort/disruption: low–medium (policy + brief workflow step). 2) Tighten escalation triggers — What it is: lower the threshold and clarify when frontline staff must escalate AI anomalies to a review team; What it fixes & effect: closes gaps where borderline failures are ignored, improving early containment; Effort/disruption: low (adjust thresholds, communications). 3) Standardize incident reporting & rapid triage — What it is: one short form and a 24‑hour triage rule so every AI incident is recorded consistently and prioritized; What it fixes & effect: turns ad hoc near‑misses into usable data for fixes and reduces repeat occurrences; Effort/disruption: low (form + short training) to medium if a triage rota is created. 

Indicators (name; one‑line definition; data source; how to read movement; analyst priority): 1) High‑risk decision error rate — % of AI‑assisted decisions in the incident logs that caused or nearly caused a material error (source: incident logs & report summaries); rising = actionable problem, falling = improving; (analyst priority #1: quick extract/backtest helpful). 2) Recurring failure‑mode frequency — count of incidents by the same failure category over rolling 30 days (source: incident logs + WP1 classifications); rising = persistent root cause; falling = remediation working; (analyst priority #2: needs coding/cleaning). 3) Time‑to‑detection — median hours between event and entry into the incident log (source: incident timestamps); rising = monitoring weakens, falling = detection improving. 4) Severity‑weighted incident score — simple weighted count where severe incidents count more (source: incident logs + reported impact); rising = higher aggregate risk, falling = lower risk.

Slide‑ready bullets (Slide 1 — Problem, questions, interventions): Problem: AI‑assisted decisions expose the organization to operational and reputational losses because governance and monitoring are uneven and incidents are recurring. Key questions: Which failure modes matter most; why do they happen; which 2–3 fixes reduce risk fast; how will we track progress? Slide‑ready bullets (Slide 2 — Indicators & Day‑10 view): Indicators we will track: High‑risk decision error rate; Recurring failure‑mode frequency; Time‑to‑detection; Severity‑weighted incident score. What leaders will see at Day 10: a 1‑page risk snapshot with the top 3 failure modes, baseline values for the 3–4 indicators, and a scored shortlist of 2–3 recommended interventions ready for a pilot decision.
